This is f*cking wild. NVIDIA co-founder Jensen Huang:

He floated a 1,000× increase in the energy needed for computing. Then he said his estimate could be off by orders of magnitude.

The reason he gave at Stanford is more interesting than the number. Software used to sit idle until you opened it. He sees more of it generating new work continuously in the background.

More background work → More model calls → More compute → More power

You can see a small version of that problem in an agent workflow. A bot can spend tokens searching, drafting, and retrying all morning and still leave you with zero claims you can publish.

Bookmark the two-minute clip for Huang’s explanation of what happens when AI keeps working between prompts.

A random guy asked Grok Bot to create the dumbest viral video possible.

Recently I’v been getting rid of my subscriptions. I’ve built my own email client, calorie tracker and a few other apps that I’ve been using daily.

I didn’t want a crappier version of the app that I used, I wanted a better version that adds features that I’m missing and removes the bloat I don’t care for.

Every app now has an MCP server so that I don’t need to click around, but just tell Grok Bot, Codex, or any other harness I currently use to pass information to it or fetch information from it.

Most of them also support WebMCP or MCP apps, so I actually never need to leave my harness - e.g. drafting and sending an email can happen right inside a chat, fetching information is just as easy.

Not every app uses AI, but every app is agent-ready, meaning that agent can access the information I defined to be accessible.

And because I use these everyday, every improvement, change or bug fix is just a prompt away.
